This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,

L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Codeine, the closest morphinan analog in the evidence set, has an absolute oral bioavailability of 80.5% in healthy subjects; hydromorphone shares the morphinan scaffold, 4,5-epoxy bridge, N-methyl group, and phenolic C3 substitution, supporting F ≥ 20%.
Other opioid analgesics in the evidence set had oral bioavailability values above the 20% threshold: pentazocine ~0.68–0.70, meperidine 0.80, and meptazinol 27.9% in cirrhosis.
No supplied record provides affirmative evidence of F < 20% for hydromorphone or a close analog; all relevant opioid F values exceed 20%.

evidence_gaps: No direct hydromorphone absolute oral bioavailability record is present in the supplied cards; the prediction relies on structural and pharmacological class transfer.
No matched oral-versus-intravenous hydromorphone exposure data in healthy subjects or a relevant disease population is available.
Codeine differs from hydromorphone at C3 (methoxy vs phenol) and C6 (hydroxy vs ketone), which may alter first-pass metabolism.
Several supporting opioid values were measured in cirrhosis patients and may not exactly reflect healthy-subject bioavailability, though all remain above 20%.
content.decision_summary: Hydromorphone is predicted high (F ≥ 20%) based on the high oral bioavailability of the closest morphinan analog codeine (80.5%) and other opioids (pentazocine, meperidine, meptazinol all >20%), consistent with a favorable physicochemical prior; no evidence supports F < 20%, though no direct hydromorphone record is available.
